name: Ligato VPP Agent
what_it_is: A Go-based control/management plane agent for FD.io VPP (Vector Packet Processor), built on the CN-Infra framework. It exposes VPP networking functionality via a model-driven northbound API over gRPC, REST, etcd, and Kafka, translating those calls into VPP Binary API operations via GoVPP.
components: govppmux plugin (GoVPP multiplexer for VPP Binary API)
VPP plugins: ifplugin, l2plugin, l3plugin, aclplugin, natplugin, ipsecplugin, abfplugin, srplugin, stnplugin, puntplugin, wireguardplugin, dnsplugin, ipfixplugin
Linux plugins: ifplugin, l3plugin, nsplugin, iptablesplugin
protocols: gRPC (northbound API, port configurable via grpc.conf, default 9111)
etcd (KV store for config distribution and status publishing, default endpoint 172.17.0.1:2379)
VPP Binary API via Unix socket (/run/vpp/api.sock via GoVPP)
VPP Stats API via Unix socket (/run/vpp/stats.sock)
measurement: Prometheus metrics exported by telemetry plugin (polling-interval: 30s default)
Per-node counters via VPP statseg (per-node-counters on)
KVScheduler transaction metrics and graph state
configuration: etcd.conf: etcd endpoints, dial-timeout, insecure-transport flag
vpp.conf: VPP startup config (unix sockets, plugins, DPDK disable, api-trace, statseg)
vpp-ifplugin.conf: stopwatch flag, status-publishers list (etcd, redis)
telemetry.conf: polling-interval, disabled flag, prometheus-disabled flag, skipped metrics list
supervisor.conf: process definitions for vpp and agent with executable paths and args
REST API: PUT /configuration (full NB config), GET /configuration, POST /configuration/validate
agentctl CLI: status, dump all, config get/update commands
fault_injection: VPP can be stopped independently (supervisor hook terminates agent on VPP termination)
etcd can be disconnected to simulate KV store unavailability (insecure-transport and dial-timeout configurable)
DPDK plugin disabled by default in dev image (plugin dpdk_plugin.so { disable }) — swap to hardware NIC for dataplane faults
api-trace enabled (on) allowing replay and inspection of VPP API call sequences for fault analysis
KVScheduler resync mechanism can be triggered to force full state reconciliation
modes: dev mode: ligato/dev-vpp-agent image with full toolchain and debug logging
prod mode: ligato/vpp-agent image with minimal footprint
arm64 mode: ligato/vpp-agent-arm64 image for ARM64 platforms
standalone mode: docker run --privileged with embedded VPP (no external etcd required for local config)
distributed mode: etcd-backed config distribution for multi-agent deployments
local client mode: in-process configuration without external transport (localclient_vpp examples)
constraints: Requires --privileged Docker flag (or equivalent capabilities) for VPP to access kernel networking and hugepages
VPP Unix sockets (/run/vpp/api.sock, /run/vpp/stats.sock, /run/vpp/cli.sock) must be accessible within the container — agent and VPP must share the same process namespace or volume
etcd must be reachable before agent starts for KV-store-backed deployments (no built-in retry beyond dial-timeout)
DPDK plugin is disabled in dev/prod images by default; hardware NIC passthrough requires host DPDK configuration and hugepage allocation
KVScheduler enforces strict dependency ordering — misconfigured object dependencies cause transactions to be held in pending state, not silently skipped
Status publishing to Redis requires redis endpoint configuration (referenced in vpp-ifplugin.conf status-publishers but not included in default dev image config)
docker_services: etcd: external dependency, typically run separately (e.g. quay.io/coreos/etcd) on host at 172.17.0.1:2379
notable_absences: No docker-compose.yml in the repository root or docker/ subdirectories — orchestration is via direct docker run or Kubernetes manifests in k8s/
No built-in web UI — management is via agentctl CLI or REST API only
No native Kafka consumer configuration files included in dev image (Kafka is supported via CN-Infra but not pre-configured)
No TLS configuration for gRPC or etcd in default dev image (insecure-transport: true)
No built-in traffic generation or load testing tooling
